blocks.raw: <Tip>The water-cement ratio is your strongest lever to control concrete strength and durability. Every project in the Philippines should specify w/c ≤ 0.50 for coastal or aggressive environments and w/c ≤ 0.55 for normal exposure. Proper 7-day curing is non-negotiable in tropical climates.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={[ "Confusing w/c ratio with water content. A w/c = 0.50 means 0.5 kg water per 1 kg cement, not 50 kg water per m³. Lower w/c always means stronger concrete if the mix is properly proportioned.", "Assuming 7-day strength equals 28-day strength. Concrete at 7 days is typically 60–75% of 28-day strength. Design is always based on 28-day strength; early testing is for quality control only.", "Using unit weight 2,000 or 2,300 kg/m³ instead of 2,400 kg/m³. This error propagates through load calculations and self-weight estimates. Standard normal-weight concrete is 2,400 kg/m³.", "Neglecting curing in hot, dry conditions. In the Philippines, poor curing in tropical heat causes severe drying shrinkage cracking and reduced long-term durability, even if initial 28-day strength is adequate." ]} />
